The key takeaway is not a specific percentage point but the stability of the negative conclusion: realistic MCP faults do not become much easier just because the backbone is larger.4d:T5c6,Ψ-0.6 is an 8B-parameter autoregressive transformer with a single unified vocabulary. It serializes multiple modalities into one sequence: RGB images, text, camera pose, depth, optical flow, and point tracks.
Key mechanisms:
- Streams of Thought: explicit multi-step sequences interleaving text/images with geometric and motion abstractions. These intermediates function as writable working memory produced by the model itself.
- Any-to-any prompting: tasks are expressed by choosing what token blocks are given vs predicted and in what order. Different orderings correspond to different inference pathways (e.g., image pair→pose; image+pose→novel view).
- Counterfactual world modeling: given a specified motion/displacement, the model predicts flow/geometry, generates the resulting scene, and then answers questions by interpreting its own predictions—reasoner and imaginer are the same model.
- RL for representation-adaptive reasoning: intermediate generations (which modalities to emit and their content) are treated as policy actions optimized end-to-end from task rewards, unlike VLM agents that call fixed external tools.
From a foundation-model angle, the most important missing-to-verify details (not present in the provided excerpt) are: tokenization/quantization of non-text modalities, mixture ratios and objectives during pretraining, and the RL stabilization constraints (e.g., KL to a reference, behavior cloning, curricula) to avoid capability collapse.4e:T5fc,The method replaces the embedding domain from the unit sphere S^{d-1} to the probability simplex Δ^{d-1}.
- Start with a frozen multimodal encoder f(·) producing pooled features h_u∈R^d.
- Add a lightweight shared adapter g_θ (linear or 2-layer MLP) to produce logits z_u.
- Two matched-capacity heads:
  (1) Euclidean/spherical head: e_u = z_u / ||z_u||_2, scored by cosine similarity.
  (2) Simplex head: p_u = softmax(z_u) ∈ Δ^{d-1}, scored by negative Total Variation distance: s_TV(u,v)=-(1/2)||p_u-p_v||_1.
- Training remains a symmetric in-batch InfoNCE (DPR-style); the only change is the output projection and the scoring function.
The paper’s argument is geometric: cosine on the sphere is invariant to rotations and sign flips, creating many equivalent solutions where cross-modal matching can be satisfied while allowing global distribution shifts between modalities. Simplex constraints (nonnegativity + unit mass) remove much of this symmetry and force both modalities to allocate probability mass over the same coordinates, effectively calibrating them. Softmax projection also introduces invariance to global logit shifts.
To isolate geometry from capacity, they compare Euclidean vs simplex using identical adapters, and further contrast an Euclidean cross-attention variant (XAttn) against ReTreever-style simplex outputs. They also introduce RelGap, a geometry-adjusted modality-gap metric that normalizes centroid separation by within-modality spread to make comparisons across domains more meaningful.4f:T7c8,The method has three main pieces. The first is the streaming interleaving format. For ASR, the sequence alternates incoming speech chunks with incremental text corresponding to words whose end times fall into each time window, with a small lookahead. For TTS, the paper compares two formats. Fixed-ratio interleaving pairs a fixed number of text tokens with a fixed number of speech frames, which is simple but poorly matched to actual acoustic boundaries. Time-aligned interleaving instead advances in words, adds word-level lookahead, and uses alignment information to define speech chunk boundaries during training. The authors choose the time-aligned version because it reduces mismatch between linguistic units and acoustic realization.

The second piece is backbone selection. Uni-Stream is built on the VibeVoice family because its TTS and ASR variants are architecturally close and, crucially, use the same speech tokenizer. That shared discrete speech space makes unification much cleaner than combining models with incompatible codecs or token inventories. The unified model is a single decoder-only LM that takes a task token followed by interleaved text and speech chunks.

The third piece is the two-stage training recipe. The authors first adapt separate TTS and ASR models to their streaming formats. Then they initialize Uni-Stream from the adapted TTS model and jointly train on both tasks. Two auxiliary objectives are introduced during unified training: synthesis anchoring, which preserves TTS quality under joint optimization, and recognition distillation, which helps the unified model acquire ASR behavior more reliably. This is a carefully asymmetric design. Starting from TTS initialization gives a strong generative prior, but ASR needs extra guidance, while joint training can still erode synthesis quality unless it is explicitly anchored. The paper also adds representation probing across tasks, modalities, and layers to study what is actually shared internally.50:T592,The most important findings are relational rather than headline numbers. First, in streaming TTS adaptation, time-aligned interleaving yields lower TTS WER than fixed-ratio interleaving, which justifies the final data format choice. Second, the unified model reaches performance comparable to task-specific streaming models on both ASR and TTS, which is the central empirical claim: unification does not lead to a large collapse in either direction. Third, ablations show that the training recipe matters. Removing synthesis anchoring hurts TTS preservation; removing recognition distillation weakens ASR learning. Fourth, on the data side, the transcript-voting plus word-level alignment pipeline retains roughly 40,000 hours of Emilia-EN after filtering, and the authors plan to release voted transcripts and word timestamps for multiple corpora. Fifth, the probing results show that speech and text representations remain distinct across layers, while ASR and TTS representations are closer in lower layers and separate in upper layers. That result is more informative than a pure benchmark table because it explains how shared parameters can coexist with task specialization.

The paper is not centered on extreme scale. Its strongest empirical contribution is the combination of a workable training recipe, a large aligned dataset, and a representation analysis that clarifies what “unified” really means in practice.51:T41a,For a quick but useful read, start with the model overview and Figure 1. The key is to understand how both streaming ASR and streaming TTS are serialized into one interleaved sequence, especially the word-level lookahead and chunk-boundary logic in time-aligned TTS. Then read the training section with attention to why the authors do single-task streaming adaptation first and unified training second, and what failure modes synthesis anchoring and recognition distillation are meant to prevent. Finally, read the representation probing section; it carries more insight than a standard auxiliary analysis because it addresses whether joint training truly merges modalities internally.

If time is limited, the best order is: sequence format and Figure 1, unified objectives and ablations, then probing figures. Around 25–35 minutes should be enough for the main ideas. If you want to go deeper, the appendix on alignment and boundary handling is worth reading because reproducibility of time-aligned streaming TTS depends heavily on those details.52:T4c2,They propose TEM (Transformer Energy-based Model):
- Define the energy in a latent space instead of pixel space to reduce effective sampling dimensionality and improve mixing.
- Use a ViT-style transformer as the energy network, with modern stability-oriented components (RoPE, QK normalization, SwiGLU, RMSNorm/AdaLN-like conditioning) rather than classic EBM-specific constraints like spectral normalization.
- Multi-layer energy extraction: read out energies from multiple transformer layers and sum them, so different depths impose complementary constraints (local texture vs global semantics), reducing the burden on a single scalar head.
- Train with a contrastive / approximate maximum-likelihood gradient: positives from data, negatives from the model’s own short-run Langevin dynamics, using persistent chains initialized from Gaussian noise.
- Sampling/training engineering: step-size vs noise tuning, persistent buffers, and explicit latent/representation alignment choices to make high-res training workable.
The overall design choice is to avoid diffusion/flow’s fixed generative trajectory and instead rely on a stronger energy landscape plus better sampling, with quality traded for test-time steps.53:T84c,技术方案有三部分，彼此是联动的。1）Constraint-Preserving Mini-Batch Admission。作者没有沿用“等整个 train batch 满足所有约束再一起放行”的做法，而是允许 mini-batch 提前 admission。关键难点是，提前放行会不会把后续 batch capacity 用光，导致最终 train batch 无法满足配比或 quota。为此论文引入 progressive readiness targets 和 feasibility guards。前者允许早期 mini-batch 的来源构成偏离最终 train batch，只要求 rollout 进度达到一个逐步收紧的 readiness target；后者在每次 admission 时检查剩余容量是否仍足以满足未完成来源的 quota，从而保证最终可行。相比线性 target，作者强调早期 target 应更宽松，以减少被慢源拖住的等待。2）On-Demand Trajectory Data Access。作者认为 sample-level 存储粒度不适合 RL 训练消费方式，于是把轨迹拆成 independently addressable atomic units，再按训练拓扑重组访问。TP ranks 共享输入，CP ranks 只需要 sequence slice，多模态 encoder 的消费边界又可能不同于 backbone；因此数据不应按“样本”整体搬，而应按消费者需要的最小单元组织和拉取。admission 之后，payload retrieval、packing、delivery 按 micro-batch 消费顺序增量进行，并与训练计算重叠，减少 critical path 上的串行等待。3）Multimodal Encoding Deduplication。针对 GRPO 风格 RL 中同一 prompt/同一图像视频输入对应多条 trajectory 的情况，作者指出共享原始存储并不能消除训练时重复 encoder forward。KnitTrans 在 mini-batch 内对 unique multimodal input 只编码一次，把编码结果复用给多条 trajectory，并在反向时聚合这些 trajectory 对 encoder 的梯度。这个设计抓住了 RL 里“多 rollout 共享条件输入”的结构性冗余，和普通 supervised multimodal training 不同。整体上，论文的创新不在单个算法公式，而在把 admission、storage layout、execution schedule、encoder reuse 放进同一条 rollout-to-training pipeline 里联合优化。54:T4a3,The paper studies a systems bottleneck in LLM RL that directly affects learning quality: the rollout-to-training handoff. This is not merely a data movement issue. It determines which trajectories enter training, when they become visible to the optimizer, and how stale the policy becomes before updated parameters reach rollout workers. The paper isolates two coupled problems. First, batch-level admission constraints—such as source-mixture ratios and partial-rollout completion quotas—create a train-batch admission barrier if the system waits for a full train batch before admitting any data. In disaggregated execution, this adds extra parameter-version lag beyond ordinary off-policy delay, which the authors call architectural staleness. Second, trajectory payloads are large and heterogeneous: token IDs, per-token auxiliary metadata, and multimodal inputs. Existing sample-centric storage and retrieval do not match the actual consumption pattern of distributed training, causing redundant reads, unnecessary transfers, and serialized preparation on the critical path. The paper asks how to preserve RL training constraints while making this handoff both fresher and faster.55:T413,This is not a pretraining paper in the narrow sense, but it is relevant to anyone working on large-scale online training. Its main contribution is conceptual as much as practical. It separates algorithmic staleness from system-induced architectural staleness and shows that admission policy alone can materially change learning quality under the same RL algorithm. That matters for RLHF, reasoning RL, online data generation, and any future setting where training consumes freshly produced data rather than a static corpus. A second contribution is methodological: the paper does not treat throughput as the only systems metric. It connects freshness, feasibility of batch composition, topology-aware data access, and multimodal encoder reuse into one coordinated pipeline. In terms of impact, this looks like a strong systems paper rather than a new optimization method: it does not change the RL objective, but it reduces the quality gap between disaggregated and colocated training at very large model scales and under multimodal workloads.56:T80c,KnitTrans has three tightly connected components. (1) Constraint-preserving mini-batch admission. Instead of waiting until an entire train batch satisfies all batch-wide constraints, the system admits mini-batches early. The difficulty is feasibility: early admission from faster sources can consume too much capacity and make the final train batch impossible to complete under source quotas or rollout-progress requirements. To address this, the paper introduces progressive readiness targets and feasibility guards. Progressive targets allow early mini-batches to deviate from the final train-batch composition, as long as rollout progress reaches a gradually tightening target. Feasibility guards check, at each admission step, whether the remaining capacity is still sufficient to satisfy all unmet quotas. This is the key mechanism that breaks the admission barrier without violating end-of-batch constraints. (2) On-demand trajectory data access. The paper argues that sample-level storage is a poor fit for distributed RL training. It stores trajectory payloads as independently addressable atomic units, then reorganizes access according to the actual training topology. Tensor-parallel ranks share inputs, context-parallel ranks consume sequence slices, and multimodal encoders may have different placement from the backbone. Therefore, data should be fetched at the granularity required by each consumer, not by sample boundaries. After admission, retrieval, packing, and delivery proceed incrementally in micro-batch consumption order and overlap with computation. (3) Multimodal encoding deduplication. In GRPO-style RL, multiple trajectories often share the same multimodal input. Shared storage alone does not remove repeated encoder forward passes during training. KnitTrans encodes each unique multimodal input once per mini-batch, reuses the representation across all consuming trajectories, and accumulates their gradients for the encoder update. The novelty is not a single formula but a coordinated redesign of the rollout-to-training path.57:T569,Experiments are run on a 256-GPU cluster with models ranging from 235B to 671B total parameters. The workloads include agentic RL and multimodal RL, under both disaggregated and colocated architectures. The headline result is that, in disaggregated training, KnitTrans reduces architectural staleness by up to 93% relative to train-batch admission, substantially narrowing the learning-quality gap to colocated execution. The paper also isolates the admission mechanism itself: while preserving all data-source quotas, KnitTrans reduces architectural staleness by 39.2% compared with a linear-target admission strategy. This is important because it shows that simply relaxing admission is not enough; the shape of the readiness target and the feasibility check both matter. On multimodal workloads, the system improves end-to-end efficiency by reducing redundant data movement, hiding payload preparation behind computation, and eliminating repeated multimodal encoder work. The abstract truncates some of the exact efficiency numbers, but the full paper appears to include ablations for each component—admission, on-demand access, and encoding deduplication—as well as breakdowns of step time, waiting time, and transfer overhead. A strong point of the evaluation is that it separates learning-quality metrics from systems metrics instead of collapsing everything into throughput.58:T503,For a skim, start with the Introduction and the main overview figure. The three ideas to lock in are the train-batch admission barrier, architectural staleness, and the mismatch between sample-level storage and distributed training consumption. Then read the method section on mini-batch admission carefully. The most important question is why progressive readiness targets can admit data earlier than linear targets without making the final batch infeasible. After that, look at the on-demand access design and focus on how atomic units map to TP, CP, and multimodal encoder consumers, and why retrieval and packing are pipelined in micro-batch order. The multimodal deduplication section is straightforward; the main thing to understand is representation reuse plus gradient accumulation. In experiments, prioritize the staleness comparison, the constraint-preservation ablation, and the multimodal step-time breakdown. Around 30–40 minutes should be enough for the main ideas. If reading more deeply, two follow-up questions are worth keeping in mind: whether earlier admission changes gradient noise or sample correlation in subtle ways, and whether the feasibility-guard framework can generalize to richer online mixing constraints such as curriculum or continual pretraining.59:T7f5,方法上，作者提出 hierarchical agent distillation，把蒸馏上下文的来源拆成两个二元变量：历史来源 H∈{T,S}，动作前缀来源 A∈{T,S}。于是得到四种配置：TT 表示 teacher history + teacher action prefix；ST 表示 student history + teacher action prefix；TS 表示 teacher history + student action prefix；SS 表示 student history + student action prefix。学生始终学习在给定 (h,u) 下匹配 teacher 的 next-token 分布，但 (h,u) 的构造方式不同。

这个框架的关键不只是列出四种组合，而是把三个原来缠在一起的设计问题拆开：第一，在哪一层跟随 student；第二，各种配置在训练中占多少比例；第三，这些比例是否应随训练阶段变化。作者采用 self-distillation 设定来控制变量：teacher 和 student 从同一 checkpoint 初始化，teacher 冻结，但 teacher 额外拿到 student 在部署时不可见的 task guidance g，相当于 privileged-information teacher。这样做的好处是排除了架构差异、模型容量差异和初始化差异，把比较集中在上下文分布本身。

从机制上看，ST 是最有意思的配置。它让历史由 student rollout 产生，因此能覆盖 student 真正会到达的状态；但当前动作前缀由 teacher 生成，因此 teacher 在 token 级监督时仍处在自己熟悉、连贯的局部轨迹上，不会被 student 的错误 prefix 绑死。相反，SS 虽然最“on-policy”，但 teacher 需要在 student 已经写偏的动作前缀后继续给监督，这时监督信号可能变得不自然、低熵或不稳定。TS 通常介于两者之间：历史仍是 teacher-clean 的，但动作前缀来自 student，已经引入局部偏移。作者还进一步研究 mixture 和 schedule：不是固定选一种配置，而是在固定预算下混合多种配置，并比较相同 on-policy 比例但不同配对方式的效果；再进一步比较前期偏 TT、后期再引入 SS 的动态课程是否优于静态混合。5a:T852,The proposed framework, hierarchical agent distillation, factorizes context generation into two binary choices: history source H∈{T,S} and action-prefix source A∈{T,S}. This yields four configurations: TT (teacher history, teacher prefix), ST (student history, teacher prefix), TS (teacher history, student prefix), and SS (student history, student prefix). The student always learns to match the teacher’s next-token distribution on the resulting context (h, u), but the way (h, u) is constructed differs across configurations.

The key contribution is not just enumerating four cases. It disentangles three design decisions that are usually conflated: where to follow the student, how much each source configuration should contribute, and whether that allocation should change over training. To control confounders, the authors use self-distillation: teacher and student start from the same checkpoint, the teacher is frozen, and only the teacher receives privileged task guidance unavailable to the student at deployment. This removes differences in architecture, scale, and initialization, so the comparison isolates the effect of context distribution.

Mechanistically, ST is the most interesting case. Student-generated histories expose the teacher to the states the student actually reaches, which improves corrective supervision. But teacher-generated action prefixes keep token-level supervision on coherent local continuations, avoiding the situation where the teacher must continue from a malformed student prefix. SS is fully on-policy, but that is exactly why it can be weak: the teacher is queried on contexts that may already be locally broken. TS sits in between: the global state is clean, but the local token prefix is student-induced and can still degrade supervision quality.

The paper then studies mixtures and schedules. Instead of committing to one configuration, it mixes TT/ST/TS/SS under a fixed budget and compares mixtures with the same aggregate amount of student-generated data but different pairings. It also studies dynamic allocation over training, such as front-loading TT and delaying SS.5b:T6e8,The experiments are organized into three stages. Stage 1 evaluates the four configurations in isolation to separate the effects of history source and action-prefix source. The main result is consistent: ST is generally the strongest standalone configuration, while SS is the weakest across the tested settings. This supports the paper’s central claim that student histories and student prefixes have very different roles.

Stage 2 studies mixed training. A useful result here is that one cannot summarize a mixture by a single “on-policy fraction.” Two mixtures can have the same proportion of student-generated histories and student-generated prefixes, yet perform differently depending on how those sources are paired across TT/ST/TS/SS. The best tested mixtures emphasize hybrid configurations, especially ST, while retaining some TT and a small amount of SS. The role of SS is subtle: it is weak on its own, but a modest allocation can still help in a mixture by exposing the student to fully deployment-like rollouts.

Stage 3 studies timing. Front-loading TT improves early learning because teacher-clean contexts are easier and more stable. Delaying SS improves later and final validation performance because fully on-policy exposure becomes more useful once the student has acquired some competence. A schedule combining both effects outperforms static allocation.

From the provided full text, the study covers three backbones and four interactive environments under a controlled self-distillation setup. The excerpt does not provide reliable parameter counts or exact score tables, so the important takeaway is the stability of the relative ordering and the interaction between mixture composition and schedule, rather than any single benchmark number.5c:T4eb,Start with the introduction and the formal definition of hierarchical agent distillation. The paper is easy to misread as just another on-policy distillation variant; the actual contribution is the separation between history-level and action-prefix-level on-policiness.

Then read the Stage 1 results carefully. The main thing to internalize is why ST consistently beats SS. A good way to think about it is to imagine a tool-using agent that has already produced a partially wrong action. Teacher supervision after that wrong prefix is not the same as teacher supervision on a student-reached state with a clean teacher prefix.

Next, look at the mixture experiments. The important point is not the exact best weight vector, but the fact that equal aggregate on-policy ratios do not imply equal training value. That is the strongest evidence that a one-dimensional policy label is insufficient.

Finally, read the scheduling section with attention to TT front-loading and delayed SS exposure. If reading time is limited, this is a 30–40 minute skim. If you want to apply it to your own pipeline, it is worth redrawing the data-generation process and checking whether your current setup already mixes these two levels without making the distinction explicit.5d:T551,Outcome-Conditioned Visual Credit has three main components. First, Relative Visual Encoding defines a context-relative visual coordinate rather than using raw image affinity. It contrasts a predictive state’s cosine affinity to image representations against its affinity to prompt-background representations, under a shared diagonal scaling. This is meant to capture whether a token is relatively more image-driven than context-driven. Second, Outcome-conditioned Evidence Calibration combines that visual coordinate with predictive features and estimates their evidential contribution from contrasts between positive- and negative-advantage responses. The key idea is that visual relevance does not automatically imply stronger updates; contribution should depend on outcome-conditioned separation and variance-aware calibration. The paper explicitly notes that if the positive and negative sides have the same visual reference mean, the visual term should contribute zero. Third, Normalized Credit Allocation converts calibrated evidence into positive, globally normalized token coefficients that modulate the original sequence advantage while preserving its sign. These coefficients are detached and plugged into GSPO-token, so the method changes within-response gradient allocation without altering the sequence-level importance ratio and clipping logic.5e:T4ac,The paper builds the case in two layers:
1) Empirical sufficiency of behavior traces: an external estimator trained only on (question, response, correctness) triples—without access to the policy’s hidden states—can match a self-estimator of comparable capacity trained on the same supervision. This suggests confidence is largely identifiable from observable behavior.
2) Formal equivalence to RL value learning: define confidence as the conditional probability of a correct final outcome given the information available along the generation trajectory (question + generated prefix). In RL terms, this is a value function V(s)=E[return|state]. With binary correctness reward, V(s) is the probability of eventual correctness; with continuous quality rewards, V(s) is expected quality.
Algorithmically, Critic-as-Confidence (CaC) reuses the RL critic trained during PPO as the confidence estimator. For critic-free RL variants (the paper mentions GRPO), they fit a value model post hoc on rollouts and use it similarly. Because the critic can be queried at intermediate prefixes, CaC provides step-/prefix-level confidence, enabling early termination and confidence-guided decoding/selection.5f:T691,PRISM has two coupled components. First, it constructs multi-solution supervision with submodular curation. For each prompt, the system gathers candidate solutions from multiple teachers and selects a subset that is both correct and diverse in terms of reasoning-feature coverage. The important point is that diversity is defined semantically, not lexically: trajectories are mapped to discrete reasoning features, and the selected subset maximizes coverage rather than surface variation. Second, the model is trained and sampled with Gaussian noise injected into a small set of special-token embeddings. Without curated multi-solution supervision, this would behave like ordinary embedding noise. With that supervision, however, different noise draws become learned latent routing signals that steer generation toward different valid trajectories.

The theoretical analysis interprets the perturbation as a stable regularizer on the Hessian of the loss with respect to embeddings, under small-noise assumptions. That helps explain why the method does not rely on aggressive stochasticity. The design choice is also deliberate: perturbing special-token embeddings is cheaper and more localized than injecting noise broadly into hidden states or logits, and it creates a consistent train-test interface. Relative to prior work, PRISM differs from inference-time diversity methods because it does not force variation only at decoding time; it differs from generic noise regularization because the noise is paired with explicit multi-mode supervision; and it differs from plain multi-solution SFT because it adds a mechanism for controllable mode selection within the learned support.60:T5e1,The evaluation has three parts. First, on open-ended writing benchmarks including WritingPrompts and BookMIA, across two open-weight model families, PRISM achieves the best generation quality in every model-benchmark setting while also delivering the strongest or near-strongest semantic diversity. The claimed result is not a simple quality-diversity tradeoff, but an outward shift of the frontier. Second, on eight verifiable math and code benchmarks, PRISM finds more correct solutions under the same inference budget, indicating improved sampling efficiency rather than merely more varied wording. Third, in RL post-training for math and code, the authors show that standard SFT initialization leads to rapid rollout collapse, whereas PRISM checkpoints preserve broader exploration and continue to uncover correct programs during policy optimization.

The most important ablations are the component-wise ones: curated multi-solution data alone, stochastic modulation alone, and the full combination. The paper’s central claim is that the gain comes from their interaction. Another key comparison is against inference-time diversity baselines, to show that internalized diversity is more useful than decoding-only interventions. The abstract excerpt does not expose all numeric tables, but the full-paper message is consistent: better semantic diversity without sacrificing quality in writing, more correct discoveries at fixed sample budgets in reasoning, and reduced exploration collapse during RL.61:T650,DATC defines token credit via a work-based analogy: credit is proportional to the component of the policy update ‘force’ along the reward-improving ‘displacement’ direction.

Concretely, it brings two vectors into the same actor-logit space at each position t:
- Reward direction g_t: an end-to-end surrogate gradient of the frozen reward model’s score w.r.t. the actor logits for the sampled response. Because tokens are discrete, the method uses a straight-through surrogate to backpropagate through the sampled tokens into the reward model and then back into the actor’s logit space.
- Policy update direction k_t: the gradient direction that increases the probability of the sampled token (log-prob gradient). GRPO’s response-level advantage A determines whether the update reinforces (A>0) or suppresses (A<0) that sampled action direction.

Directional credit is then d_t = ⟨g_t, k_t⟩. Under a local first-order approximation, this inner product predicts whether moving along the GRPO-induced direction will increase reward locally at that token. DATC converts this into token weights by redistributing the response-level advantage across positions using a softmax over A d / τ, producing a token-level advantage while preserving the overall sign structure. A KL regularizer constrains deviation from vanilla GRPO.

The paper also provides a theoretical link: the end-to-end surrogate gradient can be written in an advantage-weighted form consistent with REINFORCE, and d_t can be interpreted as aggregating local advantages from a linearized reward model along the sampled-action direction.62:T704,The paper first places seven theories into a common comparison frame: Star-free, AC0, TC0, C-RASP, MPC, BAPO, and Sensitivity. It translates their claims into a unified prediction matrix over a task suite designed to separate them, including Boolean tasks, graph problems, retrieval, and formal-language tasks such as Dyck recognition. Where the literature does not already provide the needed result, the authors add new theoretical constructions or separations.

The empirical side has two layers. One uses small task-specific transformers trained from scratch, with controlled choices such as positional encoding, to test both fitting and length generalization. The other probes frontier pretrained LLMs on related tasks. This split is important because it helps distinguish architectural expressivity from optimization barriers and from capabilities induced by large-scale pretraining.

Several concrete comparisons are especially informative. Theories based on hard attention cannot express global aggregation, so they predict tasks like Majority to be hard; in practice, transformers can learn them and sometimes length-generalize. C-RASP captures global aggregation by modeling attention as uniform averaging, but it misses content-dependent retrieval; the paper proves an exponential-size requirement for C-RASP on a retrieval task that softmax-attention transformers solve efficiently, and observes the same qualitative gap empirically. In the other direction, theories based on loose circuit upper bounds or communication-style abstractions with unbounded local computation predict many tasks to be feasible even when trained transformers fail to learn them. The broader message is that each theory tends to fail exactly where performance depends on a feature omitted by its abstraction.63:T497,The main empirical findings are straightforward. First, no single theory explains the full behavior of either small transformers or frontier LLMs. Second, hard predictions are much more trustworthy than easy predictions. Easy predictions often come from handcrafted constructions or loose upper bounds and therefore overstate what training will achieve. Third, Parity is a useful counterexample: transformers can fail even to fit the training data, which points to an optimization barrier rather than a pure expressivity limit. Fourth, positional encoding has a large effect on length generalization, and different tasks prefer different encodings; current theories mostly do not model this source of inductive bias. Fifth, pretrained LLMs behave differently from small transformers trained from scratch, implying that a theory of LLM behavior must include data and training, not architecture alone.

The paper also contributes new theoretical results to complete the prediction matrix and uses tasks such as Majority and retrieval to show where different abstractions break. The contribution is therefore more about systematic diagnosis than about a single benchmark number.64:T928,核心做法分两段：
1) 统一的 retrieval-head 检测与跨模态对齐分析。
- 定义：对每个样本 i，有问题 token 集 Qi、证据 token 集 Gi。对每层 l、每头 h，计算从问题位置 q 到上下文位置 t 的注意力 a_lh^(i)(q,t)。
- 校准：注意力里有位置偏好/内容偏好等与“问题”无关的成分。沿用 MMRetHead 的思路，用同一上下文但把问题替换成“无信息问题”得到 u_lh^(i,∅)，用两者差异构造 calibrated retrieval score s_lh（文中给出公式），以减少“头本来就爱看某些位置/模态 token”的伪相关。
- 排序：按 s_lh 给所有头排序，默认取 top 5% 作为 retrieval heads，并在不同任务/设置下比较稀疏性与重叠度。
- 数据设计：为了检验“模态变化但证据内容不变”，构造 AV-NIAH 成对样本：同一段背景视频中插入同一个 6 位数字作为答案，插入方式要么是音频里合成语音读出（视频不变），要么是画面中央 banner 显示 1 秒（音频不变）；问题固定为“secret number”。证据 span 通过时间段映射到对应 audio/video tokens。这样能把“内容”控制住，主要变化来自证据模态。
- 检查点跨度：分析 18 个 checkpoint，覆盖语言、图文、统一、omni-modal 模型，用来观察 retrieval heads 是否在适配新模态时被复用/保留。

2) 因果验证与基于 retrieval-head 的可训练改进。
- 因果验证：对检测到的 retrieval heads 做 targeted ablation，观察音视频检索性能下降；进一步只 ablate 跨模态共享的那一小撮头（文中称少于全部 heads 的 2%），也会显著伤害更广泛的多模态推理任务，支持“共享头是关键电路而非任务偶然”。
- 训练改进（多模态文档检索）：在 MMDocIR 这类多模态文档检索任务上，先在 document-related 任务里选 retrieval heads，然后用这些头的 question→page 注意力聚合成 page score，对候选页做排序学习（ranking objective），让相关页分数高于干扰页。关键点是：不改模型主体结构，把内部注意力当作可学习的检索打分通道，并用检索监督直接塑形这些头的注意力分布；同时展示了对 layout retrieval 的迁移增益（即便没有显式 layout 监督）。65:T726,The paper combines (i) a unified detection metric for retrieval heads and (ii) causal ablations plus a downstream optimization.

1) Unified retrieval-head detection with calibration.
- For each example with question tokens Q and annotated evidence tokens G, compute per-head attention from question positions to context positions.
- To remove question-independent biases (positional preferences, modality-token priors), recompute attention using an uninformative/empty question on the same context, and define a calibrated retrieval score (following MMRetHead). Heads are ranked by this score; the top 5% are treated as retrieval heads by default.

2) Controlled cross-modality setup (AV-NIAH).
- Construct paired audio-visual inputs where the evidence content is identical but presented either as synthesized speech (audio condition) or as on-screen text in a banner (visual condition), while keeping background video, insertion depth, question, and answer fixed. Map the evidence time span to the corresponding audio/video token span.
- Analyze 18 checkpoints spanning language, vision-language, unified, and omni-modal models to study head reuse and preservation during modality expansion.

3) Causal tests and optimization.
- Perform targeted head ablations to test necessity for audio-visual retrieval; additionally ablate only the subset of heads shared across modalities (reported as <2% of all heads) to test whether a compact shared circuit supports broader multimodal reasoning.
- For multimodal document retrieval (MMDocIR), select retrieval heads on document-related tasks, aggregate their question→page attention into a page score, and train it with a ranking objective to prefer relevant pages over distractors. The key idea is to treat internal attention as a trainable scorer without redesigning the whole model.66:T49d,Key findings are organized as four analyses plus an application result:
- Sparsity: retrieval scores concentrate in a small number of heads for both spoken and displayed evidence in AV-NIAH.
- Cross-modal sharing: when the same information is delivered via audio vs on-screen text, many of the top retrieval heads overlap, indicating reuse across modalities.
- Preservation: omni-modal models largely retain retrieval heads from their language or vision-language backbones, and those retained heads remain functionally important.
- Causality: ablating retrieval heads severely degrades audio-visual retrieval; ablating only the shared subset (<2% of heads) also substantially hurts broader multimodal reasoning tasks.
- MMDocIR improvement: on Qwen3-VL-8B, training the retrieval-head-based page scorer with a ranking loss improves page Recall@1 by +6.03 over the untrained scorer; gains are reported across three model families and transfer to layout retrieval without explicit layout supervision.
(Only the +6.03 figure is visible in the provided full-text excerpt; the detailed tables for absolute scores, ablation drops, and per-model breakdown should be checked in Sec.4–5.)67:T43a,Across three distilled reasoning models and three generation seeds, the strongest safety gains concentrate in a 2–3 token early window, peaking at t2; on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, gains drop to ~0 by t3/t4.
Readability increases later even when control decreases: on 8B with StrongREJECT, probe AUROC rises from 0.648 (prompt) to 0.714 (t2) to 0.750 (t4), while steering effectiveness peaks earlier.
Main safety result at t2 on 8B: fully safe CoT+answer rate on StrongREJECT-273 improves from 29.06% to 82.05%; on a SORRY-Bench-derived harmful pool, safety improves by 27.48 percentage points. REACT outperforms evaluated baselines (CAST, AlphaSteer, prompt-boundary variants) while keeping benign refusal/usefulness near baseline.
Ablation: removing the gate preserves most harmful-set gains but roughly doubles benign refusal, indicating the edit provides the benefit and the gate limits collateral damage. A norm-matched local likelihood diagnostic suggests t2 edits increase likelihood of safe continuations and decrease unsafe ones, whereas later edits can suppress both.68:T463,The analysis uses singular learning theory. The central quantity is the real log canonical threshold, or RLCT, which replaces half the parameter dimension in the leading asymptotics of Bayesian generalization and marginal likelihood for singular models. Under a local linearization of the pretrained network, LoRA becomes a low-rank trace-regression problem. Its KL geometry is governed by a forward-backward covariance built from input activations and backpropagated sensitivities at the adapted layer. If this covariance is nondegenerate on the relevant low-rank directions, the classical reduced-rank regression RLCT is recovered. If its kernel intersects those directions, additional statistically indistinguishable parameters appear, changing the singular geometry. The paper characterizes this locally through observable tangent directions plus a residual singularity, and globally through affine linear sections of determinantal varieties. A notable conclusion is that the global learning complexity need not be determined by the ground-truth stratum; singularities on other rank strata can dominate the asymptotics.69:T473,The framework has two components. GEAR, or Geometric Agreement for Latent Reasoning, constructs the next continuous input from candidate token embeddings. Starting from the sender logits, it applies temperature scaling and candidate filtering, then reweights candidates using both their probabilities and their embedding-space agreement with other candidates. This differs from Soft Thinking, which simply averages embeddings under the predictive distribution. A candidate receives more weight when it is probable and geometrically supported by other probable candidates. The second component is the H+J communication interface. The H channel maps the sender’s consumed feedback distribution into the receiver’s embedding table, producing receiver-side continuous inputs. The J channel uses a Jacobian lens to read selected vocabulary-indexed coordinates from an intermediate sender state. The sender transmits token IDs and signed readouts; the receiver reconstructs a norm-scaled residual update using its own Jacobian-lens dictionary during prefill. The first step uses embedding-layer differences between the original and unlearned models to identify tokens likely involved in the unlearning update. This turns an open-vocabulary reconstruction problem into assembly over a much smaller candidate token set. The second step ranks candidate continuations with a contrastive fluency score, combining unlearning-induced divergence with linguistic plausibility. Divergence alone tends to produce incoherent token sequences, while fluency alone becomes ordinary generation; the combined score is meant to recover sequences that are both plausible and specifically affected by unlearning. To recover multiple deleted samples, TRACE uses a two-stage design: a broad prefix exploration stage that keeps many candidate trajectories, followed by a completion stage that expands recorded prefixes into full sequences with a narrower search.","experiments":"The paper reports experiments on TOFU, MUSE, and WMDP, across multiple LLMs and six representative approximate unlearning methods. As a result, both staged training and direct mixture tuning often end up selecting a point on an acquisition–retention trade-off rather than producing a jointly strong checkpoint. Prior work observed the phenomenon empirically, but did not explain the mechanism. The key claim here is that Euclidean decoding is the wrong lens because embedding norm decay creates spurious overtaking: a low-norm token can appear to beat the source token even when the state still points in the source direction. First, heads trained on a mix of all iterations predict that tokens need under half the iterations, yet under the standard stopping rule tokens run almost e","starred":false,"priority":"p2","reading_tier":"skim","source":"arxiv","sources":["arxiv"],"published_at":"2026-10-26","category_id":"efficient","cover_url":"/covers/2610_32246.png","hf_upvotes":0,"arxiv_categories":["cs.LG","cs.CL"],"arxiv_url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32246","source_url":null,"summary":{"core_problem":"这篇工作检验的是：looped language model 里的 halting head，是否真的能把“预测上更少的迭代数”转成“实际推理时更少的计算”。作者发现，现有做法里这两者经常不是一回事。问题有两层。第一层是训练目标错位：常见的 mixture loss 训练 halting head 时，让头部看到的是各个 iteration 状态的混合表示，而不是推理时真正决定停下来的那个单一步状态，因此 head 学到的 expected halting steps 很低，但按标准 exit rule（累计停机概率过阈值）执行时，token 仍会跑到接近最大迭代数。第二层是系统层面的 batching：即便单 token 早停成立，批量生成时整批要等最慢 token，平均 token 迭代数并不等于真实 wall-clock compute。论文要解决的不是“能否做自适应深度”这个抽象问题，而是更具体地回答：halting head 的训练、停止规则和批处理执行之间到底哪里失配，失配有多严重，怎样评估才不误导。","importance":"对预训练和推理一体化研究的意义很直接。第一，它给 looped LM / recurrent-depth LM 这条线泼了一盆冷水：如果 halting 训练目标没有和实际执行路径对齐，那么 paper 里常报的平均迭代数节省，可能并不对应真实算力节省。第二，它把“训练时的概率目标”和“推理时的离散停止规则”之间的 gap 讲得很清楚，这对任何 adaptive compute、early exit、pondering 类方法都有参考价值。第三，它提醒做基座模型的人，compute-saving claim 不能只报 expected steps，至少还要报 realized steps 和 batched pass 的实际迭代深度。第四，作者给出一个不训练 halting head 就能先估计上限收益的测试，这对是否值得投入这条路线有实际价值。贡献量级不在于提出新模型，而在于把一个被默认接受的评估口径拆开，指出其中最关键的错位点，并给出更严谨的报告规范。","technical_approach":"方法上，作者做了三件事。第一，系统比较两类 halting loss。常见做法沿用 ACT 风格的 mixture loss：每个 token 在多个 iteration 的隐藏状态按 halting probability 混合，再用混合后的表示去做语言建模损失。问题在于，推理时 token 不是在“混合状态”上停，而是在某个具体 iteration 停；如果把 mixture state 换成真实停下来的单步 state，BPB 会明显变差，说明 mixture loss 在训练时给了模型一个推理时拿不到的更容易目标。第二，作者尝试 per-step loss，也就是像 PonderNet 那样对每个 iteration 都计算语言建模损失，并用 head 自己给出的停机概率加权。这样训练目标终于覆盖了真实可能停下来的每一步，但实验表明仅靠这一点还不够，因为概率权重会自然偏向后期 iteration，模型仍不愿意早停；必须再加一个很强的 early-stop prior，显式惩罚晚停，才会得到真正较低的 realized steps。作者在第 6.2 节把原因讲得很细：不是“每步监督”天然有效，而是“每步监督 + 由 head 自己决定权重”会形成一种自洽但保守的分配，导致 head 把质量预算压到更深 iteration。第三，作者把评估从 token-level expectation 推到真实执行。除了 expected halting steps，他们还测 realized steps under exit rule，以及 batched generation 时整批实际跑了多少 iteration。这个设计很关键，因为它把概率输出、离散停止规则、batch 同步等待三者分开了。论文还讨论了单序列生成时另一个常被忽略的问题：如果 token 提前停止，后续 token 在更深 iteration 还会 attend 到它，但它在这些 iteration 没有新的 KV；若不复用已停 token 的 KV，单序列场景下的比较也不公平。作者因此把 KV reuse 作为 halting 方案定义的一部分，而不是实现细节。","experiments":"实验覆盖 140M 到 1.3B 四个规模、两套文本语料、多数配置 3 个随机种子，最大迭代 cap 为 8。核心结果有几组。1）mixture-loss 训练的 halting head，预测的 expected halting steps 往往低于 4/8，但在 90% 累积概率阈值的标准 exit rule 下，realized steps 仍接近 8，也就是几乎没有真正省下计算。2）如果强行让模型更早停，质量下降很快。作者指出，一旦节省超过大约 1 个 iteration，同等参数规模下，一个没有 halting head、而是训练时随机采样深度的 sampled-depth baseline，在相同迭代预算下反而更好。这个结论很强，因为它说明 halting head 不只是“收益没想象中大”，而是在 compute-quality tradeoff 上常常输给更简单的基线。3）mixture state 与真实单步 state 的训练-推理错位可以量化：把模型从 mixture 读出改成单步读出，性能大约恶化 0.2 BPB；而作者最小和最大模型之间总共也只有约 0.24 BPB 差距，说明这个错位不是小修小补级别，而是接近一个显著的规模收益。4）per-step loss 只有配合强 prior 才有效；没有 prior 时，虽然训练形式更接近推理，但 realized saving 仍不理想。5）batching 会吃掉大部分剩余优势。按整段文本离线评估时，per-step 模型还能赢 sampled-depth baseline；但 32 条序列一起生成时，整批实际迭代深度明显高于平均 token 深度，优势大多消失。6）作者还复现分析了已发布的 Ouro，发现它在 batched setting 下同样失去大部分节省。7）单序列生成若复用已停 token 的 KV，halting 的优势还能留下一部分；但即便如此，也打不过一个专门训练成固定约 3 次迭代的 specialist。整体实验逻辑很完整：先证伪常用指标，再定位 loss The paper formulates row-wise PTQ as posterior inference over a discrete product codebook and interprets existing greedy solvers as zero-temperature, hard-decision message-passing procedures. This makes it easier to reason about quantization error compensation, Hessian coupling, and uncertainty over codeword assignments in one framework. For pretraining-oriented readers, the indirect lesson is that deployability at very low precision depends not only on model size and weight statistics, but also on how weight distributions, activation covariance, preprocessing rotations, and codebook design shape the downstream discrete inference problem.","technical_approach":"MPQ starts from the standard weight-only PTQ objective: for each output row, choose quantized block codewords to minimize the calibration reconstruction error under X. Because the quadratic term contains off-diagonal structure from XᵀX, the best codeword for one block depends on choices made by other blocks. Instead of committing to one codeword immediately, the paper defines a finite-temperature Gibbs posterior over all discrete assignments, where lower reconstruction energy gives higher posterior probability. Existing solvers correspond to a hard, zero-temperature limit that discards near-optimal alternatives. MPQ uses a two-stage solver: finite-temperature vector approximate message passing first propagates soft posterior information across blocks, then the posterior is converted into a hard initialization and refined with exact block coordinate descent. The design keeps the PTQ setting intact: no retraining is required, but the solver explores uncertainty before final commitment.","experiments":"The experiments cover Llama, Qwen, and Mistral models under 2-bit, 3-bit, and 4-bit weight-only quantization, including scalar grids and structured vector codebooks such as E8P12. MPQ is reported to match or improve over strong solver baselines including GPTQ, LDLQ, and BCD on perplexity and zero-shot accuracy. The largest gains appear in the hardest low-bit regimes, especially 3-bit scalar quantization and 2-bit lattice quantization. At 4-bit precision, the benefit is expected to be smaller because the codebook is less restrictive and greedy errors are less costly. The paper also includes theoretical analysis of the asymptotic behavior of the VAMP solver and the role of preprocessing in finite-temperature inference. The provided content does not include full numeric tables, so exact improvement margins should not be stated here.","reading_guide":"Skim time: about 30 minutes. Then read the message-passing formulation, which is the main conceptual contribution: it explains why GPTQ, LDLQ, and BCD can be viewed as zero-temperature hard-decision methods. In the method section, focus on the interface between the VAMP soft-posterior stage and the BCD refinement stage. In the experiments, prioritize the low-bit tables, especially 3-bit scalar and 2-bit lattice settings, followed by preprocessing ablations. obligation，例如上下文是否被正确保留、工具调用是否按原生接口执行、状态是否跨轮持久、权限和安全约束是否生效、日志和 trace 是否足够支持审计。第二是统一 trace 表示。不同 harness 的原生日志格式差异很大，作者用 Trajectory Tracing 模块把原生执行记录重建到共享的 Trace IR，同时保留 Most agent benchmarks collapse model capability, prompting, context management, tool wiring, execution control, persistence, and safety into a single end-task score. That makes it hard to tell whether a failure came from the model or from the surrounding system. The authors aim to measure harness reliability as a first-class property, with explicit failure attribution, while preserving each harness’s native behavior rather than forcing a fully standardized runtime.","importance":"This is not a pretraining-method paper, but it matters for anyone studying the pretrain-to-posttrain interface in agentic settings. The main contribution is conceptual and infrastructural: separate task success from mechanism correctness. That separation is useful for tool-use LLMs, SWE agents, computer-use systems, and any setup where execution traces may later feed back into training or evaluation.","technical_approach":"$4a","experiments":"The evaluation spans 4 harnesses, 9 models, 95 tasks, and 3,420 selected executions. A second important number is that 31.1% of runs complete the task successfully while still violating at least one harness criterion. This is the clearest empirical argument in the paper: visible success can coexist with hidden system unreliability. plan-and-execute、OpenAI Agents SDK，以及另一套主流框架。作者想分离两个因素：模型尺度和框架级错误处理。全文的一个关键判断是，框架层的 retry、异常传播、结果校验和恢复逻辑，可能比 backbone 大小更影响实际鲁棒性。","experiments":"关键结果有三点。第一，在校准后的 MCP 故障下注入实验中，20B 和 120B 两档 gpt-oss lookahead。TTS 侧比较了两种格式：fixed-ratio 和 time-aligned。fixed-ratio 按固定 token/frame 比例切块，简单但和真实发音边界脱节；time-aligned 则按词推进，并给后续若干词 lookahead，训练时用对齐信息决定每个 speech chunk 的边界。作者发现 time-aligned 更适合流式 TTS，因为它把文本窗口和声学边界绑得更紧，减少了 chunk 切分带来的韵律和发音错误。\n\n第二是 backbone 选择与输入表示。作者基于 VibeVoice 家族来做统一，原因不是它“现成可用”这么简单，而是 TTS 和 ASR 变体在架构上足够接近，尤其共享同一套 speech tokenizer，这让统一训练时的离散语音表示空间是一致的，避免了两个任务各自用不同 codec/tokenizer 带来的接口错位。统一模型的输入序列以 task token 开头，后接交错的文本和语音 chunk，用单一 decoder-only LM 建模。\n\n第三是两阶段训练。先分别把 task-specific 的 TTS 和 ASR 模型适配到各自的 streaming 格式，再用 streaming TTS 模型初始化统一模型，之后做 joint training。这里有两个关键辅助目标。一个是 synthesis anchoring，用来约束统一训练后不要丢掉原有 TTS 合成能力；另一个是 recognition distillation，用蒸馏方式帮助统一模型吸收 ASR 能力。这个设计反映了作者对训练不对称性的判断：统一模型从 TTS 初始化，天然更容易保住生成端能力，但识别端需要额外信号拉起来；同时 joint training 又会反过来伤害合成质量，所以需要 anchoring 去稳住。文中还做了表示探针，比较不同层、不同任务、不同模态的隐藏状态相似性，用来回答“统一训练后内部是否真的融合”这个问题。","experiments":"实验里最重要的不是单一分数，而是几组对照关系。第一，流式 TTS 的数据格式比较中，time-aligned interleaving 比 fixed-ratio 有更低的 TTS WER，这直接支撑了后续统一模型采用 time-aligned 方案。第二，统一模型和各自 task-specific streaming 模型相比，在 ASR 和 TTS 上都做到“接近而非明显落后”，这是全文最核心的结果。摘要和正文给出的结论是 comparable to task-specific models，说明统一没有出现常见的双任务明显塌缩。第三，训练消融验证了两阶段训练和两个蒸馏/锚定目标的必要性：去掉 synthesis anchoring，会更容易损伤 TTS；去掉 recognition distillation，ASR 学习会更弱。第四，数据侧作者构建了 transcript voting + word-level alignment 流水线，对 Emilia-EN 做过滤后保留约 40,000 小时训练数据，并计划公开 Emilia-EN 的投票转写，以及 Emilia-EN、GigaSpeech、LibriSpeech 的词级时间戳。第五，表示分析发现 speech/text 表征在各层都保持区分，没有因为双向任务统一而塌成单一共享空间；ASR/TTS 任务表征则在低层更相似，在高层逐渐分开。这组结果比任务分数更有研究价值，因为它解释了为什么共享骨干仍能保住任务特化能力。\n\n从全文可见，这篇工作更强调系统性验证，而不是追求极端规模。给出的关键信息集中在训练流程、数据构造和表示分析上；如果要找对预训练研究最有用的数字，4 万小时 time-aligned 英语数据是最重要的一项，另外就是 unified 与 task-specific 的性能差距被压到较小范围内。","reading_guide":"泛读时建议抓三部分。先看方法总览和 Figure 1，理解 streaming ASR 与 streaming TTS 的交错格式到底怎么写成一个序列，尤其注意 time-aligned TTS 里的 word lookahead 和 speech chunk 边界。再看训练部分，重点是为什么先单任务 streaming reasoning 的 RL 阶段有方法论价值。它提醒了一点：细粒度 credit assignment 不能只靠表示相似度或注意力强弱来拍脑袋决定，必须结合 outcome 条件来解释。这个思路对语言模型也有启发，尤其是在 process supervision 稀缺、只能拿到 response-level reward 的场景里。若以后把类似方法迁到纯文本 reasoning、tool-use RL、甚至 pretrain 中的 token reweighting，关键不是找到“重要 token”，而是找到“在正负结果对比下，哪些 token 特征真正携带可学习证据”。","technical_approach":"方法叫 Outcome-Conditioned Visual Credit，分三步。第一步是 Relative Visual Encoding。作者不直接用 token Calibration。作者把视觉坐标和 predictive features 组合成特征向量 z=[v;ρ]，再利用正 advantage 与负 advantage 响应之间的统计对比来估计各坐标的 evidential contribution。这里有两个关键点：一是 credit 来自 outcome contrast，而不是来自视觉关联本身；二是用 regularized 的 The authors also derive an observable lower bound, TPR_lb, so the true causal detection rate is constrained by two measurable quantities rather than inferred from TPR_mc alone. Standard calibration checks compare probabilities against frequencies; this evaluation checks self-consistency across latent explanations.
